On Monday I will be a guest on the [First Word in Sport](https://www.youtube.com/@FirstwordinSport) podcast to discuss the forthcoming World Cup and some memories of previous World Cups. While researching this assignment, I realised just how many times England have been robbed, either during qualifying or the competition proper:

# 10. USA employ a Haitian who scores the winner (1950).

Joe Gaetjens, never a U.S. citizen, capped for Haiti both before and after playing for USA.

# 9. Ronaldinho flukes a cross into the top corner (2002).

Because he was a great player and he reacted like he meant it, everyone has to play along with the idea that he meant it. No he didn't. Seaman.


# 8. Qualifying comes down to who can thump Finland and Luxembourg by the most (1978).

Finland 1-4 England
England 2-1 Finland
Luxembourg 1-4 Italy
England 5-0 Luxembourg
Finland 0-3 Italy
Luxembourg 0-2 England
Italy 6-1 Finland
Italy 3-0 Luxembourg

UEFA finally just changed its qualification format to include pre-qualifying like everyone else. 

# 7. Poland keeper has the game of his life (1974).

Mythical stories growing up. But this really was a pasting. Shots 36-2.

# 6. Stupid format means England go home undefeated (1982).

Maybe it's my age, but 1982 feels like a bit of a forgotten World Cup for England. 

# 5. Koeman escapes red card then scores free kick (1994). 

Do I not like that!

# 4. Ronaldo gets Rooney sent off (2006).

# 3. Simeone cheats to get Beckham sent off (1998). 

# 2. Lampard goal miles over the line (2010).

"Thanks a lot, Sepp Blatter!"

# 1. Maradona hand of god (1986).



We do "getting cheated" better than any country in the world!

Add cheeky reference to 1966, definitely no dodgy decisions there (Rattin red card & dubious goal in final).
